main_body: A flat grass ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a repeating tuft pattern; it is terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none; flat ground texture with no distinct top band and front face
evidence: Terrain kind: a seamless grass ground patch with no standing volume. The column scan shows a repeating 16-row tuft cycle (mid green with light and dark tuft pixels) and no top/front structure. Nothing is drawn as a front elevation, side elevation or top-down slab, so the 3/4 contract does not apply and nothing in the drawing violates it.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 80 colours and 26 per tile for the reference grass. It uses about 4 green steps (dark, mid, light, highlight) in a rigid 16px repeat that reads as a mechanical stamp, with identical tuft shapes and orange marker pixels at regular intervals. Dark pixels are tinted green (0% neutral), so the tone is fine. There are no 5x5 flat fills, but the tufts are sparse and uniform, so the texture lacks the clump variety, soil grain and per-blade shading of the Beodeul grass. It would look noticeably thinner and flatter than the reference next to it.
